A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT-Bridge and ScaleQM+ study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching the renumbered scoring appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement-learning, bridge-task evaluation, ablation and reasoning-quality scoring results in Tables 1–11.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and adds qualitative comparisons of model-generated bridges in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The ScaleQM+ construction, Qwen2.5-Math-7B bridge model, joint leap identification and missing-step generation, and downstream insertion procedure remain unchanged. Section 2.2 adds a dataset-choice rationale without changing the method.

E1.justification: The training corpora, six mathematical benchmarks, five logical-reasoning benchmarks, ScaleQM+ evaluation and RL task are retained. The new case study reuses the dice problem from Figure 1(a), adding no distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: New Appendix I includes GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-PRO as zero-shot bridging comparators alongside Qwen2.5-Instruct-7B/72B and CoT-Bridge. Comparator membership in the quantitative benchmark and RL tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented splits, training budgets, decoding settings, evaluation metrics and RL settings remain unchanged. Appendix I presents case-level outputs using the existing zero-shot bridging approach, without specifying a changed testing protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix I extends the existing dice illustration into a comparative case study examining bridge placement, omitted planning content and redundant insertions. The step-removal, bridging-position and PRM-filtering analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging four outputs per problem and retain the same discussion of generation and scoring variability. No new seed information, independent training-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–11 and the existing figures are unchanged. Appendix I adds qualitative outputs: GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-PRO supply the missing sum-count calculation, while Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct also inserts a redundant step.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 retains the same completeness predicate and leap-repair formalization. Appendix H retains identical precision, recall, redundancy and position-aware BERTScore definitions; no mathematical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about formalizing Thought Leaps, improving reasoning through bridging, logical-task generalization, and compatibility with distillation and RL. The headline performance gains are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 now explicitly describes ScaleQuestMath as an approximation to ideal CoT, justified by its relatively complete structure. Appendix I interprets a redundant Qwen72B insertion as illustrating the existing aggregate redundancy finding. Appendix B's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The front-page project access address changes from the ccai-lab GitHub Pages site to the zju-real site. Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter and prompt documentation is otherwise retained; the PDFs establish no new code or data release.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix A add references and brief discussion covering hidden-state steering, self-correction, self-braking and broader RL applications, including SEAL and EasySteer. The central positioning around reasoning completeness remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes local grammar and terminology corrections, fixes Figure 2 references, adds a short dataset rationale and acknowledgements, and inserts the case-study appendix. The former Appendices I and J become J and K; the main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Appendix I adds boxed model-output comparisons. Tables receive limited label, emphasis and spacing changes, including replacing GapBridge with CoT-Bridge in Tables 4 and 11. The existing four figures and eleven quantitative tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity through the explicit ScaleQuestMath rationale, corrected cross-references and consistent method labels. The new comparative case study makes localization and redundancy differences more concrete. Its single-example scope and unchanged quantitative evidence limit the overall gain.
